sources_considered.why: Primary announcement of Meta's voice functionality.
Primary announcement of downloadable models and on-device capabilities.
Establishes that the reasoning models were available to Plus subscribers before the post.
Independent contemporaneous evaluation of o1-preview, including its advantages and limitations.
The February retention study is outside the selected quarter. Retention also does not by itself establish a durable barrier.

evidence_items.locator: Section Meta AI Now Has a Voice, first paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: The voice section announces spoken conversations with Meta AI across its messaging products. This supports the existence of a voice competitor, without establishing equal quality.

evidence_items.locator: Takeaways, paragraph describing the 1B and 3B models
evidence_items.explanation: The release documents downloadable small models supporting local summarization, rewriting and instruction following. It supports expanding alternatives for some tasks, not full parity with ChatGPT Plus.

evidence_items.locator: Section How to use OpenAI o1
evidence_items.explanation: Reasoning-model access was already part of Plus before the post. Together with e4, this establishes a capability difference beyond the voice exception.

evidence_items.publisher: Karthik Valmeekam, Kaya Stechly and Subbarao Kambhampati; arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 3, Evaluating LRMs on the Original Test Set
evidence_items.explanation: The independent evaluation found a large advantage on its original Blocksworld tasks. It also found deterioration on harder instances, so the result establishes specific differentiation rather than general reliability or a lasting moat.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not establish whether any advantage was durable.
No contemporaneous study measures how much the reasoning advantage affected typical Plus subscribers' willingness to pay.
The reviewed evidence does not quantify switching costs.
